transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-12 10:00 PST
Duration: 43 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Asterion ML), Liam O'Neill (Asterion Product), Sara Gomez (Asterion Infra)

Summary section (auto): quick notes: today we go over the week of test results, discuss pinning to model v2.1 vs v2.0, fallback behavior and canary plan.

[00:00] Maya Chen: all right hi everyone, thanks for joining our weekly pilot sync. How are we doing on time? We have about 45 minutes.
[00:22] Priya Kapoor: good, thanks. We ran the inference jobs overnight and got some numbers but we want to go through the quality side first.
[00:30] Diego Ramos: yeah i'll share screen in a sec — sorry mic's a little low — but the key things: we compared catalog model v2.0-quant and v2.1-fp16 across your prompt set.
[00:48] Liam O'Neill: quick q, is v2.1 the one with the new attention kernel? I thought that was v3.
[00:56] Diego Ramos: no, v2.1 has the optimized rotary caching, it's the fp16 variant, v3 is a different family. sometimes the naming gets messy in the catalog, sorry for that.
[01:12] Sara Gomez: on infra, i just want to flag we hit a QPS spike that blew past our baseline, so if the pinned model changes latency we need autoscale thresholds tuned.
[01:25] Priya Kapoor: okay good point. now for the results — we saw v2.1 improved median latency by about 12% but the 95th percentile was similar to v2.0. quality-wise, v2.1 produced slightly fewer hallucinations on the medical triage prompts.
[01:48] Diego Ramos: yes that's what we'd expect; float16 reduces quantization noise vs the quantized v2.0. cost per token is roughly 18% higher on v2.1 in our infra.
[02:05] Maya Chen: let's unpack that: improvement in quality and median latency but higher cost. Customer's success criteria leaned on recall and low hallucination for safety. Priya, does that trade-off make sense?
[02:21] Priya Kapoor: yes quality is number one, but we have a hard budget ceiling. If the cost delta is 18% we need to see if batching or caching can recoup that. Also we need deterministic rollbacks in case of regression.
[02:40] Diego Ramos: we tried prefix caching on the larger intents, kv-cache improved throughput for repeated session flows by about 22%. That can offset some cost. I can attach the raw traces.
[03:00] Liam O'Neill: can we pin per-route? e.g., sensitive intents pinned to v2.1 and others stay on v2.0?
[03:10] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood's routing supports per-route model overrides. You can also set canary percentages. Diego, can you outline a minimal canary policy?
[03:22] Diego Ramos: sure — minimal would be: 5% traffic to v2.1 for 4 hours, monitor latency, error-rate, hallucination metric (we infer with heuristics), then ramp to 25% if stable for 24 hours. fallback: immediate auto-fallback to v2.0 on threshold breach.
[03:45] Priya Kapoor: what are the thresholds we should use?
[03:49] Diego Ramos: recommend 10% P95 increase or any new critical classification errors above baseline. We can tune the thresholds after the first run.
[04:05] Sara Gomez: about the auto-fallback — does the system preserve session KV when switching back? We can't drop context mid-call.
[04:14] Diego Ramos: good question. We keep KV per session if models are compatible — there is a compatibility table — but if you switch to a different architecture we'd need a cold start. For v2.0<->v2.1 it's compatible.
[04:30] Priya Kapoor: there were a few prompts where v2.0 gave more verbose but safe answers and v2.1 compressed them and missed some nuance. I can share examples.
[04:43] Maya Chen: please do — those will help us tune decoding settings and temperature, and maybe use n-best reranking.
[05:00] Liam O'Neill: competitor question — we looked briefly at Anthropic and Anthropic's family had better safety in one of our evals. How does Redwood help with safety regression monitoring?
[05:12] Diego Ramos: we wire your eval sets into the quality monitors. Redwood Optimize can alert on regression against your golden prompts and trigger rollbacks or notify the team.
[05:25] Priya Kapoor: what's the latency hit when we enable cross-request batching? Some of our flows are low-latency.
[05:32] Diego Ramos: batching helps throughput but adds queuing latency. We recommend adaptive batching: small batches for low-latency routes and larger batch sizes for high-throughput background jobs.
[05:50] Maya Chen: ok let's go through the shared spreadsheet Diego sent last night. (screen shares)
[05:55] [06:15] Diego Ramos: table 1: median latency v2.0 = 82ms, v2.1 = 72ms. p95 v2.0 = 260ms, v2.1 = 255ms. tokens per second marginally higher on v2.1. Quality score (heuristic) v2.0 = 0.78, v2.1 = 0.83 on your triage set.
[06:40] Priya Kapoor: those heuristics — what's included?
[06:43] Diego Ramos: lexical overlap, entity preservation for high-risk slots, and hallucination detector. It's not perfect but it flags regressions.
[06:55] Priya Kapoor: we need human review on top of heuristics for launch decisions.
[07:00] Maya Chen: agreed. We'll run the A/B and then sample the disagreements for manual triage.
[07:10] Liam O'Neill: can we pin model versions in the API call to ensure reproducibility? If we update our codebase we don't want silent model drift.
[07:20] Maya Chen: yes — Redwood supports explicit model_version parameter in the request. You can pin at route-level or call-level. Also we support immutable model tags for audits.
[07:33] Sara Gomez: audit logs — we need to keep token-level logs for SOC-2. Does Redwood provide that for private deployments?
[07:40] Diego Ramos: yes, for Dedicated and Private we can ship token-level cost/latency breakdowns and audit logs to your SIEM or s3 with KMS encryption. We'll share the docs.
[07:55] Priya Kapoor: earlier you mentioned rollback semantics — what happens to in-flight requests when a rollback is triggered?
[08:02] Diego Ramos: in-flight continue on the old variant until complete; new requests after the switch go to fallback. So no mid-request model swap.
[08:15] Maya Chen: there's also a 'graceful-degrade' mode where we route long-running sessions to a compatibility tier. Might be useful for triage.
[08:25] Liam O'Neill: for the next run, how do we track hallucination metrics automatically?
[08:30] Diego Ramos: we can wire a lightweight classifier to tag likely hallucinations, then sample those for manual review. We'll include the classifier config in the repo link.
[08:45] Priya Kapoor: sample size — how many prompts should we use for the A/B to be statistically meaningful?
[08:50] Diego Ramos: for our major intents, aim for at least 1k examples each; for rare intents we can do focused evals.
[09:03] Maya Chen: quick pause — any blockers from infra side?
[09:07] Sara Gomez: VPC peering window next Friday morning is okay, but we need Redwood to confirm IP ranges and a short runbook.
[09:15] Maya Chen: okay we'll send the runbook and ranges after the call.
[09:20] Liam O'Neill: about catalog naming confusion — could we get a one-pager mapping model aliases to capabilities? It's hard to keep track.
[09:28] Diego Ramos: absolutely, we'll produce a catalog matrix that maps family, v numbers, quantization, and recommended routes.
[09:35] Priya Kapoor: one more nuance: some prompts showed non-deterministic tokenization differences between runs — could be stemming from pre-tokenizer updates.
[09:45] Diego Ramos: noted. We'll lock tokenization version in the pinned model config during the trial.
[09:52] Maya Chen: all right let's make decisions: do we pin to v2.1 for sensitive intents and keep v2.0 as default?
[10:00] Priya Kapoor: yes that's our preference, pending the A/B results and the cost-vs-offset calculation with caching.
[10:08] Liam O'Neill: agree. Also want the canary plan and rollback playbook before we flip any traffic.
[10:14] Maya Chen: Diego will own the playbook. We'll schedule the canary for next Wednesday if everything lines up.
[10:22] Diego Ramos: i'll draft the playbook and include thresholds, monitoring dashboards, and the rollback CLI commands.
[10:30] Priya Kapoor: will you include the step to snapshot model version and config in the audit log?
[10:34] Diego Ramos: yes. We create an immutable deployment artifact id.
[10:40] Maya Chen: wrap up: recap quick — A/B benchmark run by Redwood, share results by 3/18; customer to upload prompts by 3/14; canary playbook by Diego 3/20; VPC peering on 3/22.
[10:55] Liam O'Neill: sounds good.
[11:00] Maya Chen: thanks everyone. we will follow up with links in crm and send calendar invites for the canary kickoff.
[11:10] [END OF TRANSCRIPT]
